canvas-01-1.description: The main map of Sheet 1 occupies the lower right of the page, below the key map and index, and is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. It covers the northern edge of Englishtown along North Main Street, from Dey Street at the bottom of the sheet north across Spotswood Creek to the fork where an unnamed road runs off to the northwest and Old Middletown Point Road runs to the northeast. Road to Old Bridge leaves Old Middletown Point Road toward the north at the upper right corner, and the dash-dot borough limits line crosses the sheet diagonally. The area is thinly built: a scattering of frame dwellings with sheds, coops and auto houses lines North Main Street south of the creek and the north side of Dey Street, and a few more dwellings stand along Old Middletown Point Road and in the angle of Road to Old Bridge. Spotswood Creek winds across the middle of the sheet from west to east, with a steel bridge carrying North Main Street over it. Much of the part is open land divided into large lots, with block numbers 1, 2, 3 and 17 printed across it. Dey Street along the bottom edge is the boundary with Sheet 2, which draws the blocks south of it, and the area west of North Main Street at the bottom belongs to Sheet 4. The two small insets at the left of the same page, separate places on Road to Old Bridge north of town, are not part of this map.
notes: The road running northwest from the fork is lettered Not Named; it is Wilson Avenue today.
Old Middletown Point Rd is Gordons Corner Road today; Road to Old Bridge is Pension Road at this junction.
North Main is Main Street today.

The fitted scale (3.83 px/ft) is about 3 percent below the other sheets; the junction of Old Middletown Point Rd and Road to Old Bridge is drawn about 12 m closer to the fork than the modern junction.

Printed sheet 1. Top half is the key map (600 ft to an inch, colour-coded sheets 1-4) with water facilities, fire dept note, location map, index of specials and legend: not georeferenced. Lower half at 100 ft: part 1 (right) North Main from Dey Street north to the fork of the unnamed road (now Wilson Avenue) and Old Middletown Point Road (now Gordons Corner Road), with Road to Old Bridge (now Pension Road), Spotswood Creek; part 2 (upper left inset) The Pineland summer boarding house, C.W. Westervelt, on Road to Old Bridge, located 2 miles N of P.O.; part 3 (lower left inset) chicken farm on Road to Old Bridge, located 1 1/2 miles N of P.O.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: The Pineland summer boarding house (C.W. Westervelt), Road to Old Bridge, located 2 miles N of P.O. (no street junction: one road with no named crossing, outside the reference box; needs hand-picked control from the modern road and parcels about 3 km north of Englishtown (Pension Road / Englishtown Road corridor); location along the road not determinable from the sheet).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: chicken farm on Road to Old Bridge, located 1 1/2 miles N of P.O. (no street junction: one road with unnamed lanes crossing, outside the reference box; needs hand-picked control; position along the road not determinable from the sheet).

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the centre of Englishtown east of Main Street, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north at the top. It runs from Dey Street at the top to Tennent Avenue at the bottom, bounded on the west by North and South Main Street and reaching east past Irvington Avenue to the borough limits, with Spotswood Brook crossing the upper right corner. Cross streets are Dey, Center, Pine and Mechanic, with Water Street entering from the west at Main, and Harrison running north and south through the middle. The Main Street frontage is the business district: general stores, a drug store, bakery, barber, pool room, dry goods and grocery stores, a confectionery and post office, an auto sales room and auto repair shop, a garage, a tailor, and buried gasoline tanks. Behind it on Mechanic Street are a synagogue and the University Middy House, a middy blouse factory. The public school and the First Presbyterian Church stand on the east side of North Main between Pine and Water. East of Harrison, Berger, Gordon and Co. made umbrella handles and the De Lux Novelty Co. celluloid novelties, with a celluloid vault. The rest of the sheet is frame dwellings with stables, coops and auto houses on long lots, more open toward the east, where Center and Mechanic run out past the dash-dot borough limits line. A pump house and auto supply stand at the lower right near Tennent Avenue.
notes: Mechanic is Hamilton Street today; Irvington is Irving Place.
North and South Main are Main Street today.
The same stream is lettered Spotswood Creek on Sheet 1 and Spotswood Brook here.
Dey ends at Harrison; Center continues east of Harrison only as a narrow lane past the borough limits.

Scale 100 ft. Centre of town east of Main: N. and S. Main, Dey, Center, Pine, Mechanic (now Hamilton Street), Tennent Av, Harrison, Irvington (now Irving Place); Water St stub. Public school, Presbyterian church, synagogue, Berger Gordon umbrella and De Lux Novelty celluloid works, Middy factory. One part.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the south side of Englishtown, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north at the top. Tennent Avenue runs along the top edge from South Main Street east past Harrison Street and Irvington Avenue, and the sheet reaches south to the Pennsylvania Railroad and beyond it to the borough limits. South Main Street crosses Weamaconk Creek on a steel bridge beside an old mill and dam, then divides into Manalapan Road to the southwest and Railroad Avenue to the southeast. Railroad Avenue turns east at Millhurst Road and ends at Station (Railroad Av.), which runs south to the depot and freight house. Much of the sheet is taken up by the Weamaconk Millpond, which spreads east and south behind the houses of Tennent Avenue and Railroad Avenue in a long irregular arm with an island. Along the railroad stand the industries: the Theodore K. Hann basket factory with its store houses, conveyor and engine, and the Rooney and Ely hay, feed, coal and fertilizer yard with store houses, feed house, hay storage and grain house beside Millhurst Road. J. R. Lewis's nightgown factory is on Tennent Avenue. The rest is frame dwellings with stables, sheds, coops and auto houses, thickest along Railroad Avenue and Manalapan Road, with large open lots between the pond and Tennent Avenue. A windmill and tank stand at the upper right.
notes: Manalapan R'd is South Main Street today; South Main north of the fork is Main Street.
Railroad Av is Park Avenue today, both the southeast arm and the eastward arm past Millhurst Rd.
Millhurst R'd is Conover Street today; Station is Station Street; Irvington Av is Irving Place.
The railroad is lettered Penn. R.R.; OpenStreetMap calls the line the Freehold Secondary.

The fork of Manalapan Rd and Railroad Av and the corner of Railroad Av and Station were not used as control: the modern junctions lie 12 and 19 m from where the sheet draws them (Station Street now meets Park Avenue further west).

Scale 100 ft. South of Tennent Av: S. Main, Manalapan Rd (now South Main Street), Railroad Av (now Park Avenue), Millhurst Rd (now Conover Street), Station (Railroad Av.) (now Station Street), the Weamaconk Millpond, Pennsylvania RR with depot, Hann basket factory, Rooney & Ely feed, Lewis nightgown factory. One part.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 covers the west side of Englishtown, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north at the top. North and South Main Street run down the right edge, from above Center Street to below Tennent Avenue, and Water Street runs west from Main to a steel bridge over Weamaconk Creek, continuing beyond it as Lasatta Avenue to the left edge of the sheet. Wood Avenue comes in from the northwest and meets Lasatta Avenue at the west end of the bridge. Weamaconk Creek crosses the sheet from north to south through the middle. The built-up part is the Main Street frontage and both sides of Water Street: the Village House hotel, a bank, a tinsmith, a meat market, stores and dwellings, the Knights of Pythias hall, a Ford service station of concrete block, and the Sanford Memorial M. E. Church on South Main Street. The Englishtown Fire Co. house stands near Tennent Avenue, and a note at the lower right lists its apparatus. West of the creek a few dwellings line Wood Avenue and Lasatta Avenue, and the rest of the sheet is large open lots with block numbers 11, 16, 19, 20 and 22. Center, Pine, Mechanic and Tennent are drawn only as short stubs east of Main, which is shown on Sheet 2.
notes: Mechanic St is Hamilton Street today; North and South Main are Main Street.
Wood Avenue now meets Lasatta Avenue and Water Street at two junctions west of the creek; the junction drawn at the bridge was not used as control.

All detected control points lie along Main Street; two derived points west of the creek, from a similarity fit to them, hold the scale across the sheet to the scale along Main Street. The western half is placed by that scale and rotation, not by its own control.

Scale 100 ft. West of Main: N. and S. Main from above Center St to below Tennent Av, Water St, Lasatta Av, Wood Av, Weamaconk Creek; Ford service station, K. of P. hall, Village House, Sanford Memorial M.E. church, fire department. One part.
